title: Fluorescence probing of glycation-induced conformational changes and aggregation in fibrinogen
content: Non-enzymatic glycation of plasma proteins generates advanced glycation end products (AGEs) and is associated with metabolic and cardiovascular disorders (CVDs). Fibrinogen, a key plasma protein involved in coagulation, is susceptible to glycation, which may alter its structure and promote abnormal clot formation. In this study, we investigated methylglyoxal-induced glycation in fibrinogen using LED-induced autofluorescence (LED-IAF) as a label-free detection approach and validated the associated structural alterations using complementary biophysical methods. In vitro glycation induced conformational changes in fibrinogen, accompanied by protein unfolding, increased aggregation propensity, and formation of AGE-modified fibrinogen. LED-IAF sensitively distinguished glycated fibrinogen from its native form, consistent with the findings obtained using established biophysical analyses. To explore the clinical relevance of these observations, a preliminary analysis was performed using plasma samples from patients with CVD and healthy subjects. Immunodetection of AGEs revealed significantly higher levels of glycated fibrinogen in plasma samples of CVD patients, indicating that fibrinogen modifications observed in vitro are also detectable in clinical samples. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that glycation substantially alters fibrinogen structure and aggregation behaviour and support LED-IAF as a sensitive, label-free approach for detecting fibrinogen glycation. The observed increase in AGE-modified fibrinogen in CVD plasma further supports its potential as a candidate biomarker, warranting validation in larger, well-characterized clinical cohorts.
